versions.changelog: Add section 'The queue you do not control': when the work source has no conditional write, the claim is not transactional and the golden rule inverts - failure must be terminal and explicitly written, claims confirmed by read-back, orphans reclaimed by TTL.

1.0.0 — Initial release.

A ticket queue becomes draft PRs from an agent that cannot merge — enforced at the permission level, not by asking nicely: the token carries contents:write and pull_requests:write only, so gh pr merge fails.

The load-bearing ideas: a conditional server-side ack is the strongest lock you can get on a queue; red means no PR AND no ack, which makes the queue self-healing; the grounding gate runs on both client and server; idempotency is keyed per headSha; and a skeptical second agent must try to refute a destructive verdict before it stands — doubt never escalates.

If anyone asks whether a comment is automated, the answer is yes.
